dedupe_keys.name: disaster information reachability of medium wave am broadcasting reception surveys after the 2024 noto peninsula earthquake shoji 2026

description: This preprint defines Disaster Information Reachability as the capacity to deliver necessary information to those who need it when they need it, and examines medium-wave AM broadcasting on the Noto Peninsula after the 2024 earthquake, which caused widespread power outages, communication failures and road disruption in a peninsula with limited transport links. In September 2024 the author ran a mobile reception survey from Kanazawa to Suzu City and a fixed-point survey in Suzu City with commercial radio receivers and passive receivers including HOOPRA. Stations in Niigata, Toyama, Akita and Tokyo were clearly received, local NHK Kanazawa stations suffered noise, and the still-operating high-power NHK Radio 2 network provided multidirectional reception through maritime propagation. The paper argues AM warrants reassessment in preparation for a Nankai Trough megaquake. Producer: Eiichi Shoji, submitted 12 August 2026 and revised 13 August 2026. Coverage: Noto Peninsula and route to Kanazawa. Access: free arXiv preprint; only the abstract page was read, because no HTML version exists. Licence and cost: free to read; licence arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence (the paper; no open reuse licence). Caveats: a single author's survey with numbers not seen here, and it is a preprint under review. Simulation uses: the reception results give evidence for coverage and redundancy in emergency-communication models of broadcast networks. Related record: the HOOPRA medium-wave AM disaster case study (case_study-hoopra-medium-wave-am-radio-disaster-japan).
